overall_structure.value: After hot rolling to an 82% reduction and water quenching, the HR82 microstructure consists of equiaxed FCC austenite grains containing a large fraction of first-order annealing twins, together with micron-sized polygonal (Nb,Mo,W)C particles, submicron spherical (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and homogeneously dispersed nano-sized κ-carbides.

morphology.value: equiaxed grains with a large fraction of first-order annealing twins (Σ3 (60°〈111〉) boundaries)

grain_size.value: 18.80 μm (mean grain size excluding twin boundaries); 7.02 μm effective mean grain size when annealing twin boundaries are included

lattice_distortion.value: highest KAM (local strain concentration) of the three samples, with the most extensive high-orientation-gradient regions

homogeneously distributed in the austenite matrix; volume fraction ~0.198%

source.reason: Sections 4.2 and 3.2 describe the (Nb,Mo,W)C/austenite interface behaviour (debonding, microvoid nucleation), κ-carbide/austenite shearing, and the planar-glide slip band → microband evolution for HR82.

coherence.value: incoherent — the (Nb,Mo,W)C particles cannot be sheared and are bypassed by dislocations through the Orowan mechanism
coherent and shearable — gliding dislocations shear the κ-carbides forming anti-phase boundaries

interaction_type.value: intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particle–matrix strain/stress concentration, particle debonding and microvoid formation

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: The intergranular hard (Nb,Mo,W)C particles cause strain/stress concentration at their interfaces due to deformation discrepancy with the austenite matrix and act as preferential nucleation sites for microcracks; this concentration is partially alleviated by debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and subsequent microvoid formation. Abundant ductile dimples on the HR82 fracture surface indicate the intergranular particles had virtually no detrimental effect on toughness.

slip_behavior.value: Predominant dislocation planar glide despite the high SFE: at low strain, homogeneously distributed arrays of planar slip bands and Taylor lattices (crossing non-coplanar {111} slip traces) form. With increasing plastic strain the slip bands become more closely spaced; for HR82 the slip band spacing at εe = 0.1 was 68.05 ± 8.91 nm, much finer than HR45/HR68. Refinement saturates at ~50 nm, after which microbands with ill-defined and then distinct boundaries develop (faster and earlier for HR82 due to its finer grain size).

phase_evolution.value: A single fully austenitic matrix; nano-sized κ-carbides form by spinodal decomposition and subsequent ordering during fast cooling (water quenching) without a further aging treatment. No strain-induced martensite or β-Mn reported for HR82.

interface_notes.value: κ-carbide cutting by leading dislocations produces glide-plane softening and preferential glide paths, favoring planar slip bands and Taylor lattice formation; further deformation rotates the Taylor lattice and generates microbands delineated by dislocation walls of GNDs.

validation_against_experiment.value: The calculated SFE (~73 mJ/m2) is high, yet planar glide deformation substructures were observed, explained by the glide plane softening effect from κ-carbide shearing.

model_name.value: Olson and Cohen thermodynamic SFE model

model_note.value: The high SFE (~73 mJ/m2) would normally favor cross-slip and dislocation cell formation, which was not observed; instead planar glide occurred due to κ-carbide-induced glide plane softening.

unmapped_findings: HR82 retained a large fraction of first-order annealing twin (Σ3 (60°〈111〉)) boundaries: the twin boundary fraction was 52% (determined by length relative to total length of boundaries with misorientation >15°).

Crystal structure of the (Nb,Mo,W)C particles was identified as face-centered cubic (FCC) with a calculated lattice parameter of 4.36 Å (determined from the HR68 submicron particle by EDS/SAED, applies to the same MC-type particles present in HR82).
The stacking fault energy of the steel (all hot-rolling states including HR82) was calculated to be ~73 mJ/m2 using the Olson–Cohen thermodynamic model.
HR82 slip band spacing at εe = 0.1 was 68.05 ± 8.91 nm, the finest of the three reductions, indicating faster development of deformation substructures with increasing hot-rolling reduction.
Microbands were observed at εe = 0.2 in the HR82 sample, earlier than in HR45, attributed to its finer grain size.
